skill.name: conductor-status
skill.description: Display Conductor project progress, active tracks, blockers, and next actions from local project status files.
skill.summary: Summarizes Conductor project status from local planning documents.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static analyzer flagged Markdown backticks and fenced examples as Ruby shell execution, but the reviewed file contains no executable scripts or shell invocation. The skill reads local Conductor planning files and formats project status output; no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior was found.

remediation.suggestion: Clarify in the README or skill description that backticked text is documentation and that the skill does not execute shell commands.

remediation.issue: The skill relies on local project files that may contain private planning details.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users that status output is generated from local Conductor files and should be reviewed before sharing outside the workspace.

- Count total tasks (lines matching `- [x]`, `- [~]`, `- [ ]` with Task prefix)

content.value_statement: Conductor projects can become hard to scan when tracks, tasks, and blockers are spread across several files. This skill turns local Conductor planning documents into a clear status report with current focus and next actions.
actual_capabilities: Checks whether Conductor project files are present before reporting status.
Reads local product and track documents to summarize project progress.
Counts completed, in-progress, and pending tracks and tasks.
Identifies the active track, current phase, and next pending task.
Reports blockers noted in tasks, dependencies, or failed verification work.
Provides full-project, single-track, quick, and JSON-style output formats.
limitations: Requires an initialized Conductor file structure in the current workspace.
Depends on consistent task markers and track metadata in local files.
Does not create, modify, or execute project tasks by itself.
May miss blockers that are not written in the expected Conductor files.

use_cases.title: Review project progress before implementation
use_cases.description: Generate a concise view of active tracks, completion counts, and next tasks before starting work.

use_cases.title: Prepare a team status update
use_cases.description: Convert Conductor planning files into a readable summary of progress, blockers, and near-term actions.

use_cases.title: Inspect one track in detail
use_cases.description: Focus on a single track to review its specification, implementation phases, and pending verification work.

prompt_templates.title: Show Project Status
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for the default report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conductor-status to show the current project status for this workspace.

prompt_templates.title: Check One Track
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review of a known track identifier.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conductor-status for track TRACK_ID and summarize the current phase, blockers, and next task.

prompt_templates.title: Find Immediate Next Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conductor-status to identify the active track and list the next three actions I should take.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Progress And Blockers
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before a handoff or planning meeting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use conductor-status with detailed output. Highlight progress by track, unresolved blockers, dependency risks, and verification work still pending.

output_examples.output: A full project report with total tracks, task completion counts, an active track summary, next actions, and any blockers found.
A single-track report with track metadata, specification summary, phase progress, related commits, and the next pending task.

output_examples.input: Give me a quick Conductor status.
output_examples.output: A short summary with the project task count, completion percentage, active track, and current task.

best_practices: Run the status check before changing task files so the report reflects the current plan.
Keep task markers and metadata consistent across Conductor files.
Review generated status before sharing it because local planning files may contain private details.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill in repositories that do not use Conductor project files.
Do not treat the report as complete when track metadata or plans are outdated.
Do not share generated status externally without checking for confidential project information.

faq.question: Does this skill execute shell commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill describes how to read local Conductor documents and format status output.

faq.question: Which files does it expect?
faq.answer: It expects Conductor files such as conductor/product.md, conductor/tracks.md, and track-specific plan, metadata, and spec files.

faq.question: Can it show one track only?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a track identifier to request a focused status report for that track.

faq.question: Can it report blockers?
faq.answer: Yes. It looks for written blockers, incomplete dependencies, and failed verification tasks in the Conductor files.

faq.question: Does it modify project files?
faq.answer: No. It is a reporting workflow and does not update tasks or metadata by itself.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
